correctness.rationale: Equal marginal variances force a deterministic second noise difference to be exactly common noise. For all other covariances Gaussian conditioning gives a potentially nonzero pole numerator; proving its conditional variance and mean cannot vanish jointly by a rank-one covariance contradiction certifies a strictly positive pole coefficient. Conditional Gaussian density near the zero denominator yields both 1/t tails and exact p=1 moment boundary. Rational covariance identities and seeded PSD examples passed 2044 finite checks; proof, not tests, handles all admissible parameters.

value.rationale: This is an exhaustive covariance-design answer for noisy unregularized extrapolation with fixed per-measurement precision: only perfectly shared randomness prevents infinite absolute first moment. The explicit rapidly vanishing but positive pole coefficient close to perfect coupling exposes a serious numerical-diagnostics trap, and the theorem gives a natural sharp boundary for deciding when common-random-number schemes need regularization. A one-shot, finite-dimensional classification has independent methodological value without claiming general multistep stochastic convergence.
